clue.text: Multitudes sign to have spymaster imprisoned

indicators.note: the sign is made to hold something, taking it within itself
locked up, so the spymaster sits inside the sign like a prisoner in a cell

parts.note: Aries the Ram is a sign of the zodiac
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign is pictured locking up a master spy, with crowds somehow involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies are huge numbers of people, so the word stands for multitudes, as in an army of fans.

clue.text: Sceptic engaged in armed robbery?

parts.note: to be at something is to be busy doing it
a heist is a robbery, often armed

explanation.surface: A doubter is caught up in a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'at heist': busy with a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist doubts or rejects belief in God, a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Lesson master put into speech

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster delivers a lesson out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches.

clue.text: Old relationship Ruby brought to an end

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pi is the fixed ratio relating a circle's circumference to its diameter
ruby is a deep shade of red

explanation.surface: A former romance with someone called Ruby is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old relationship' reads as one idea, a former partner, but it splits in two; the relationship is the circle ratio of mathematics. 'Ruby' looks like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expired has run out or finished, so it has been brought to an end.

clue.text: Put pressure on one involved in a row

definitions.meaning: to caress or rub with the hand, pressing gently
the oarsman who sets the rhythm in a rowing eight; row here is rowing a boat

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the gentle pressing action of a hand on fur; the other is the rower at the stern who sets the pace for the crew.

clue.text: Native boy appears in distress

indicators.note: the boy shows up inside the hardship

parts.note: a trial is a hardship or affliction
B is the abbreviation for boy, as in births notices

explanation.surface: A local lad is seen in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes belonging to an indigenous tribe, so native in that sense.

clue.text: Frank individuals producing subtle innuendoes

parts.note: frank means open, unconcealed: overt
ones are single people or things

explanation.surface: Plain-speaking people are, oddly, the source of hints.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are implied meanings or suggestions underneath what is said, much like innuendoes.

clue.text: Copper in Essex demolished feeble defences

indicators.note: the metal symbol goes inside the rearranged county
knocked down and broken up, so the county's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman in Essex dismisses weak alibis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' makes EXSES from ESSEX, and 'in' puts CU in the middle. Essex is an English county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Excuses are weak justifications offered to defend oneself, so poor defences.

clue.text: Commander, a bit crazy, is sectioned

parts.note: Com is an abbreviation for commander
a part is a bit or piece
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A commander, slightly mad, has been committed to a psychiatric ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sectioned' in Britain means detained under the Mental Health Act; here it means divided into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Compartmental means divided into compartments, that is, split into sections.

clue.text: Fish in burn

definitions.meaning: a trout-like freshwater fish of cold lakes
to scorch or blacken the surface of something

explanation.definitionFit: The same four letters name a cold-water fish related to trout and the verb for scorching something black.

clue.text: Renown for coppers capturing errant minor

indicators.note: the coins close round the other letters, holding them inside like captives

parts.note: copper coins, British pennies, so pence

indicators.note: straying or wandering, so the letters of minor drift out of their order

explanation.surface: Police win fame by arresting a young delinquent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins. 'Errant' rearranges the five letters of minor, and 'capturing' puts them inside the coins just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominence is the state of standing out and being well known, a close synonym of fame or renown.

clue.text: Ploughman makes lines in row

indicators.note: the lines are set inside the row of seats

parts.note: a tier is a row or rank, as of seats
L is a standard abbreviation for line, doubled for lines

explanation.surface: A farmer cuts furrows in a field, line after line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is one who tills the soil, so a farmer working the land with a plough.

clue.text: Go over and scrape it off

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for cleaning a surface: review it, then scrape the stuff away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' reads as part of 'scrape it off', but it signals the anagram of SCRAPE and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise something is to rehearse it, going over it again and again to improve.

clue.text: Workman's first wife died in supermarket

indicators.note: the wife and died go inside the shop

parts.note: a supermarket is a large store
Eve, wife of Adam, was the first wife in the Bible
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A labourer's first wife passed away in a supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a docker, a labourer who loads and unloads ships, so a kind of workman.

clue.text: Criminal damage? Museum gets woefully slim support!

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: done wretchedly or badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A museum laments a meagre level of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victoria and Albert Museum is known as the V and A; written out it gives VANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandalism is wilful destruction of property, which is criminal damage in law.

clue.text: Boundaries some defend successfully

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some borders are held against attack, as in a successful defence.
explanation.definitionFit: The ends of something are its limits, the edges or boundaries where it stops.

clue.text: Gasp like a man in gym

indicators.note: the a and the chessman go inside the gym letters

parts.note: PT, physical training, is school gym
N is knight in chess notation, and a chess piece is a man

explanation.surface: Someone panting like a man working out in a gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' means a chess piece here: N, the knight's notation. PT is physical training, the school name for gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant is to breathe in short, quick gasps after exertion.

clue.text: Object to vermin carrying decay

indicators.note: the vermin hold the decay inside them

parts.note: a pest is a creature such as a rat regarded as vermin
rot is decay

explanation.surface: Someone objects to rats spreading disease.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise an objection, so to object.

clue.text: One man begged to be moved

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for male, or man
to press someone is to urge or beg them

explanation.surface: A single man pleaded to be allowed to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks like relocated, but it means emotionally touched.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impressed means being affected or touched emotionally, a sense of moved.

clue.text: Withdraw soldier's entertainment

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers
a treat is an outing or entertainment given as a pleasure

explanation.surface: A soldier's night out is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to pull back or withdraw, especially of troops.

clue.text: High spirits leading to broken toenail

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Joy follows a broken toenail, which is an odd thing to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and excitement, a state of high spirits.

clue.text: Forceful and disagreeable when imprisoning taxmen once

indicators.note: the unpleasant word locks the taxmen up inside it

parts.note: vile means very unpleasant
IR, the Inland Revenue, was the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: Tough, nasty people lock up former tax collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK tax office until 2005, when it merged into HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means vigorous and powerful, strongly masculine, so forceful.

clue.text: Present and organise race

parts.note: to do a party is to organise or arrange it
a people or nation can be called a race

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a gift and set up a running event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is the noun, a gift, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift given to a cause, so a present.

clue.text: Fabric for belt requires input of skill

indicators.note: the belt has the skill fed into its middle

parts.note: to belt someone is to thrash them, to tan their hide
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Making a fabric belt needs some craftsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like a strap but is the verb, to beat: TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the woollen cloth woven in the checked patterns of Scottish clans.

clue.text: Agent the Spanish hold off

parts.note: a rep, representative, acts as an agent
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish agent fends off an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or keep at bay, so to hold off.

clue.text: Weird game title I authorised

indicators.note: something weird is odd or out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone approves a strange name for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or sanctioned, which is what authorised means.

clue.text: Parking by the verge is proper

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a rim is an edge or verge

explanation.surface: Parking a car beside the grass verge is the correct thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A verge in Britain is the grass strip beside a road; here it is just an edge, RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly correct and formal in manner, a sense of proper.

clue.text: Restrain Paddy

definitions.meaning: to moderate or tone down something, as when justice is softened with mercy
a paddy is a fit of anger, a tantrum

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to moderate or tone something down; the other is a bad mood or tantrum, which British slang calls a paddy.

clue.text: Moral taint engulfs sinister despot

indicators.note: the taint swallows up the left letter inside it

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a moral taint
sinister is Latin for left, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: A wicked tyrant is tainted by his evil deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' looks like an adjective on despot, but it is the heraldic left: L.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin was the Soviet dictator, a notorious example of a tyrant.
